validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE all confirmed via multiple independent origins. HVJ is India's first cross-country gas pipeline and is exhaustively documented: (1) GAIL (India) Ltd's own letter to the PNGRB Secretary dated 27.11.2018, 'Final Tariff Determination of HVJ-GREP-DVPL and DVPL/GREP Upgradation Natural Gas Pipeline Network of GAIL (India) Limited' (one of the gem.wiki page's own cited leads, chased and read directly) -- a scanned/image-only 7-page PDF with no text layer (url_verifier 200s and correctly reports every keyword missing; confirmed manually via pdftoppm 300dpi + tesseract OCR of all 7 pages). Annexure-A para 1.1 states verbatim: 'HVJ:- The Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) Pipeline (About 1800 kms, 18.4 MMSCMD), India's first cross-country natural gas pipeline, was commissioned in 1987-88, with compressor stations at Hazira (Gujarat), Jhabua (M.P.), Vijaipur (M.P.) and Auraiya (U.P.).' This is GAIL's own first-party regulatory account, independent of GEM, and confirms EXISTENCE as a formal regulatory filing (not marketing copy). (2) The current PNGRB monthly line-wise register (https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf, edition 31 May 2026; large multi-column PDF, url_verifier false-negative per the documented pattern, confirmed locally via `pdftotext -layout`) lists 'Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur -GREP- Dahej-Vijaipur HVJ/VDPL Dadri (GREP) Upgd. DVPL 2 & VDPL' under GAIL in its OPERATIONAL COMMON CARRIER section: authorised 6,169 km / operating 6,732 km / authorised+design capacity 111.3 MMSCMD / 80.3 MMSCMD supplied / 75.0% utilisation -- confirming the whole integrated system, including HVJ, is currently operating, not just historically built. A second table in the same report ('NGPL under Regulation 17') lists the same 'Integrated HVJ' asset with Design/Determined Capacity 107.0 MMSCMD -- see the Capacity finding below. (3) GAIL's own live corporate website (https://www.gailonline.com/Natural_Gas.html, verified OK, contains 'HVJ' and 'GREP') lists 'HVJ-GREP DVPL' as an active 5,433 km network component 'As per PNGRB As on 30th Jun 2026', current as of this sweep. (4) Wikipedia's 'HVJ Gas Pipeline' article (verified OK) and (5) offshore-technology.com's GlobalData-sourced marketdata entry for 'Hazira-Vijaypur-Jagdishpur Gas Pipeline' (verified OK) both independently corroborate the asset as real, GAIL-owned, and operating. PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas are both correct -- this is unambiguously a cross-country natural-gas transmission trunk line, India's flagship one. Owner1=GAIL (India) Ltd 100% is correct and undisputed across every source above -- GAIL is the sole named entity throughout its own regulatory filing and every third-party source. DUPLICATE check against the full 35-row India roster: P0925 (HVJ) is NOT the same pipe as its four siblings P0919 (DVPL-I), P3297 (GREP-I), P3298 (DVPL-II), P3299 (GREP-II) -- the GAIL tariff letter's own genealogy (paras 1.1-1.4) and the current PNGRB register both independently corroborate that HVJ (1987-88, ~1800 km core trunk), GREP-I (1997, 36in x 505 km, Vijaipur-Dadri = P3297), DVPL-I (2004, 42in x 612 km, Dahej-Vijaipur = P0919), Upgradation Phase-I/GREP-II (commissioned March 2010, 48in x 505 km Vijaipur-Dadri parallel to GREP = P3299), and Upgradation Phase-II/DVPL-II (commissioned Aug 2013, 48in x 610 km Dahej-Vijaipur parallel to DVPL-I = P3298) are five historically and physically distinct construction projects sharing a common right-of-way, now operated and tariffed as one integrated network -- exactly the granularity split this sweep's own scope guidance anticipated. Do not collapse.

Both are independent of gem.wiki and of each other (GAIL corporate publishing vs. a commercial energy-data aggregator), so tier=high. Caveat: neither source disaggregates which specific build phases sum to 2887 km -- GAIL's own 2018 tariff letter describes the original 1987-88 HVJ trunk as only 'about 1800 kms', so 2887 km most likely represents HVJ's core trunk plus at least one later-subsumed expansion (GREP and/or DVPL-I were both 'subsumed as part of HVJ' for tariff purposes per that same letter, even though GEM tracks them as separate rows) rather than the original 1987 pipe alone. This is a labeling/genealogy nuance worth noting in ResearcherNotes, not a numeric error -- the value itself is well corroborated as-is.

validity.recommendation: correct StartYear1 from 1997 to 1987 (or 1987-88 if a two-value field is available) -- 1997 is the commissioning year of the separately-tracked GREP expansion (P3297), not of HVJ itself
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC check on StartYear1. GEM carries StartYear1=1997 for P0925/HVJ. This is contradicted by every independent source found, all agreeing on 1987 (some giving 1987-88 to reflect India's April-March fiscal year): (1) GAIL's own 27.11.2018 tariff letter to PNGRB, Annexure-A para 1.1 (OCR-confirmed, see existence finding above): 'was commissioned in 1987-88'; (2) GAIL's own 2021-22 Sustainability Report Glimpses timeline graphic (same PDF as the Length finding, `pdftotext -layout` line ~165-167): 'India's first natural gas pipeline- Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) commissioned' positioned under the year '1987'; (3) Wikipedia's HVJ Gas Pipeline article (verified OK, contains '1987'): 'Construction started in 1986 and the system was commissioned in 1987'; (4) offshore-technology.com's marketdata entry (verified OK, contains '1987'): 'Commissioning Year: 1987'. Four independent origins (two of them GAIL's own primary materials) all say 1987, none says 1997. The likely explanation: 1997 is when the SEPARATE GREP expansion project was commissioned -- per the same GAIL tariff letter para 1.2, 'GREP-- Later, during the year 1997... the HVJ pipeline capacity was expanded... by laying a new 36" x 505 Km pipeline from Vijaipur to Dadri' -- and GREP is already independently tracked in the roster as its own row (P3297, Vijaipur-Dadri Gas Pipeline (GREP-I), updated 2023-07-13). It looks like HVJ's own StartYear1 was set to its expansion's commissioning year rather than its own. This is a genuine, fixable date error, not a judgment call, and warrants verdict=concern rather than a caveat.

validity.recommendation: correct EndState/Province from Madhya Pradesh to Uttar Pradesh -- EndLocation 'Jagdishpur' itself is correct and needs no change; Vijaipur (Madhya Pradesh) is a mid-route waypoint reflected in the pipeline's own name, not the terminus
validity.researcher_notes: ATTRIBUTION check on the Location cluster. GEM's EndLocation='Jagdishpur' is correct, but EndState/Province='Madhya Pradesh' is wrong -- Jagdishpur (the pipeline's own named eastern terminus, an industrial/fertilizer-plant hub in Amethi district) is in Uttar Pradesh, not Madhya Pradesh. Vijaipur, which IS in Madhya Pradesh, is a compressor-station waypoint in the middle of the route (reflected in the pipeline's own 'Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur' name), not its endpoint. Three independent sources agree: (1) Wikipedia's HVJ Gas Pipeline article (verified OK, contains 'Jagdishpur' and 'Uttar Pradesh'): 'The pipeline runs from Hazira, Gujarat to Jagdishpur (Industrial Area), Uttar Pradesh, passing through Vijaipur, Madhya Pradesh'; (2) testbook.com (verified OK, contains 'Jagdishpur' and 'Uttar Pradesh'), an independent educational-quiz site restating the same route (Hazira, Gujarat -> Vijaipur, Madhya Pradesh -> Jagdishpur, Uttar Pradesh); (3) offshore-technology.com's marketdata entry (verified OK, contains 'Uttar Pradesh'): 'starts at Arabian Sea (India) and ends in Uttar Pradesh (India)'. GAIL's own materials corroborate indirectly: its Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga trunk line (JHBDPL, Jagdishpur-Haldia-Bokaro-Dhamra) is universally described as originating at Jagdishpur, Uttar Pradesh, and ties in to this same HVJ system for gas injection -- consistent with Jagdishpur being a UP location, not an MP one. This is a genuine, fixable state-attribution error with high-confidence, multiply-independent support.

validity.recommendation: flag Capacity=107.00 MMSCMD for Update review as a probable system-total-vs-segment mismatch, consistent with the same pattern already flagged on sibling row P0919 (DVPL-I) in this sweep -- do not silently pass
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC check on Capacity. GEM's Capacity=107.00 MMSCMD for P0925 (HVJ) is IDENTICAL to the value carried on all four sibling rows in the 35-row roster that make up the same integrated system: P0919 (DVPL-I)=107.0, P3297 (GREP-I)=107.0, P3298 (DVPL-II)=107.0, P3299 (GREP-II)=107.0. This is very unlikely to be five coincidentally-equal, independently-measured segment capacities; it reads as the SYSTEM-WIDE total design capacity copied onto every constituent row rather than each project's own incremental capacity. Two independent primary/regulatory sources corroborate the aggregate interpretation, not a segment-specific one: (1) GAIL's own 2018 tariff letter to PNGRB gives the incremental capacity buildup explicitly -- HVJ alone at commissioning: 18.4 MMSCMD (1987-88); after GREP: 33.4 MMSCMD (1997); after DVPL-I: ~57.3 MMSCMD (2004); after Upgradation Phase-I: ~68.3 MMSCMD (2010); after Upgradation Phase-II/DVPL-II: combined system total ~111.3 MMSCMD (2013) -- HVJ's OWN capacity, by this account, was never 107 MMSCMD at any point; that number only appears once every later expansion project is added in. (2) The current PNGRB monthly register's 'NGPL under Regulation 17' table lists the 'Integrated HVJ' asset (GAIL, authorised length 6,169 km) with Design/Determined Capacity = 107.0 MMSCMD -- an exact match to GEM's value, but explicitly at the SYSTEM level (spanning HVJ+GREP+DVPL-I+DVPL-II/Upgradation combined), not the HVJ segment alone. This is the same finding already independently staged on sibling row P0919 (DVPL-I) in this sweep, which additionally notes the figure is now ~4 points stale versus the current PNGRB main-table authorised/design capacity of 111.3 MMSCMD. I am not proposing a replacement number for P0925 myself -- whether Capacity should be split per segment (18.4 MMSCMD for HVJ's own historical increment) or consistently labeled as the current system total (111.3, refreshed) is a judgment call for Update, and is a cross-row (not P0925-specific) data-convention question. Flagging as concern rather than a silent pass per the sweep's spec rule that a source must AGREE with the GEM number, not merely mention the pipeline -- here the two sources found actually corroborate a different quantity (the system total) than what a literal reading of the column (this segment's own capacity) would imply.

fills.researcher_notes: Diameter was genuinely blank on the sheet. Two independent sources agree on 36 inches (914.4mm): Wikipedia's infobox and offshore-technology.com's marketdata entry ('Diameter: Maximum of 36 inches'). Staged as MEDIUM tier rather than high because both sources describe 'HVJ Gas Pipeline' at the same broad grid scope as the 2887km Length figure above, which per the Length finding likely already spans more than just the original 1987 trunk -- and GAIL's own 2018 tariff letter separately documents the GREP expansion (a different, already-separately-tracked row, P3297) as also 36in pipe. So 36in is well supported as the pipeline-family's dominant/most commonly cited diameter, but is not confirmed as specific to the original 1987 HVJ segment alone as distinct from the subsumed GREP addition. Recommend a human sanity-check against a GAIL/PNGRB engineering document if segment-level diameter precision matters; otherwise safe to stage as-is given GEM's Diameter convention elsewhere in this roster is a bare inch number (P3297=36.00, P3298=48.00, P0920=48).
